_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.3 'Zero Trust in four habits' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): verify every request, assume breach, least privilege, keep checking. Requests invented around the fictional RSSO cast; the checks are the guide's: who you are, from which device, whether your role needs it.

items.text: Ben signs in to the portal from his office PC, passes MFA, and opens an application assigned to him.
items.reason: Every check passes, so the request is allowed. The point is that it was **checked**, even inside the office.

items.text: Someone signs in with Dan's correct password from a laptop the office has never seen.

facts.v: ? A password only: no second proof

items.reason: Keep checking: a login from an unusual place is blocked and reviewed. A correct password proves nothing on its own.

items.text: A staff PC on the office network asks the applicant database for all 48,000 records.

facts.v: ? A staff PC, not a person
Plan as if an attacker is already inside

items.reason: **Being inside the office network proves nothing.** Least privilege: give only the access the job needs.

items.text: Sol, on her office phone, opens one applicant's case from a network she has never used before.
items.reason: Verify every request, not once at the door: something changed, so the policy asks her to prove it is still her (MFA again), then lets her work.

items.text: Ana tries to open the portal's admin pages from her everyday account, the one she uses for email.

facts.v: ✗ Admin work uses a separate admin account, only for admin work
Admin pages answer on the admin network only

items.reason: Least privilege for admins too: a phishing email opened in her everyday account must not reach the admin pages.
